newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK sells utility remnants for 257 mln pounds.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK sells utility remnants for 257 mln pounds.

text.p: The British government sold off its remaining stakes in a slew of privatised utilities on Tuesday to raise 257 million pounds ($428.7 million) through a competitive auction organised by bankers Rothschild acting for the Treasury.
"We thought it represented a good time and a good price to sell," a Rothschild spokesman said.
In a statement, the Treasury said that 81 million shares in British Energy Plc had been sold to HSBC James Capel -- the equivalent, analysts say, to around 12 percent of the company.
The government was left holding 12.27 percent of British Energy after its dismal debut in July at 98 pence, below the first instalment price to institutions of 105 pence.

But since then shares have risen thanks to better than expected results last week as losses shrank to 53 million pounds for the half year from 169 million pounds previously confirming the trend. By 1322 GMT they stood at 147.5 pence.
The government has kept around five million shares in British Energy to cover bonus share entitlements which fall due in 1998.

The sale also included 18.8 million shares in Scottish Power which analysts say amounts to around 1.6 percent of the company, to Germany's Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, with the two stocks showing highest volumes on the market on Tuesday.

The Treasury also sold off its remaining holdings in National Grid, Northern Ireland Electricity, Scottish Hydro-Electricity, National Power, PowerGen, Severn Trent, South West Water and Wessex Water.
The Treasury had indicated in March it intended to sell the stakes by the end of the current financial year, industry sources said. ($1=.5995 Pound)
